records.issue_text: admin-group.js.es6: totalPages = Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1 is off-by-one when user_count % limit == 0 (100 members, limit 50 yields totalPages 3 when only 2 pages exist), so showingLast fails on the real last page and 'next' stays enabled; correct math is Math.ceil(user_count/limit) (or floor((user_count-1)/limit)+1).
records.rationale: The diff adds `totalPages: Math.floor(this.get("user_count") / this.get("limit")) + 1` in admin-group.js.es6. When user_count is an exact multiple of limit (e.g., 100 members, limit 50), this yields 3 pages when only 2 exist. Since `showingLast` is `propertyEqual("currentPage", "totalPages")` and currentPage is `floor(offset/limit)+1`, on the actual last page currentPage=2 ≠ totalPages=3, so showingLast is false and the 'next' action remains enabled. Math.ceil(user_count/limit) is the correct computation. The mechanism is fully verifiable from the diff.

records.rationale: The diff confirms the mechanism: groups_controller.rb previously applied limit/offset only to automatic groups (defaulting 200), but now applies `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` to all groups with no fallback to fetch more; group-members.js.es6's setupController calls model.findMembers() with the model's default limit of 50 (set in group.js `limit: 50`), and members.hbs iterates `{{#each m in members}}` with no pagination controls — next/previous actions exist only in admin-group controller. Public groups with >50 members are silently truncated with no way to page.

records.issue_text: The client-supplied `limit` parameter on the public groups#members endpoint is uncapped (`limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` in app/controllers/groups_controller.rb), allowing unauthenticated requests like `?limit=99999999` to load and serialize the entire membership of large groups (e.g., automatic trust_level_0) in a single request, enabling resource exhaustion
records.rationale: The diff adds `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` with no upper bound on the public groups#members endpoint, and unlike the old code, pagination now applies to all groups. A request like ?limit=100000000 would cause `group.users.limit(limit)` to load the entire membership for serialization in one request. The mechanism described is accurate to the diff and is a resource-exhaustion/security concern introduced by this change.

records.rationale: The diff wraps the admin group template in a new <form class="form-horizontal"> containing {{text-field name="name" ...}} and {{user-selector ...}}, with no submit handler or onsubmit prevention anywhere in the template or controller. Pressing Enter in a text input inside a form triggers native form submission, reloading the page and losing unsaved edits — a concrete regression introduced by this diff.

records.issue_text: The new admin group pagination logic (currentPage, totalPages, next, previous) has zero unit tests, which would have caught the exact-multiple-of-limit edge case.
records.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial new pagination logic (currentPage, totalPages computed properties and next/previous actions in admin-group.js.es6) yet the spec changes in spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb cover only controller endpoints, with no tests for this logic. The concern is specific and grounded; the cited edge case is plausible since totalPages = Math.floor(user_count/limit)+1 over-reports pages when user_count is an exact multiple of limit (e.g., 100 users, limit 50 → 3 pages instead of 2).

Under the advisory bar this is a style/consistency nit lacking decision relevance.

records.issue_text: totalPages off-by-one in admin-group.js.es6 (~line 13): Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1 should be Math.ceil, so when user_count % limit == 0 (e.g. exactly 100 members at limit 50) totalPages is 3, showingLast is false on page 2, and 'next' advances to an empty page 3/3; same defect surfaces after removing a member when the page lands exactly on a multiple
records.rationale: The diff shows `totalPages: Math.floor(this.get("user_count") / this.get("limit")) + 1`. With user_count=100, limit=50, this yields 3 while only 2 pages exist. `showingLast` (propertyEqual currentPage/totalPages) is false at currentPage=2, so the 'next' action sets offset to 100 and fetches an empty page 3/3. Math.ceil would be correct. Mechanism fully verifiable from the diff.

records.issue_text: usernames is singleton Ember controller state that is never reset — setupController only sets the model and addMembers deliberately doesn't clear the input — so text typed while editing group A remains when navigating to group B, and clicking 'Add' then adds those users to the wrong group (membership grants permissions); after a successful add, the retained text also invites a duplicate re-submission. Regression from the old code that derived usernames from members per model.
records.rationale: The diff confirms the mechanism: the old controller derived usernames from members per model via the removed `usernames` computed property, while the new code declares `usernames: null` as plain controller state; setupController now only does `controller.set("model", model)`, and addMembers has an explicit `// TODO: should clear the input` comment confirming the input is not cleared. If the controller persists across route entries (typical for Ember singleton controllers of that era), stale usernames can be submitted against a different group's id. The mechanism is grounded in the diff, though
